metadata.description: Validated movement quality scoring rubrics for 8 sports movements. Thresholds derived from peer-reviewed biomechanics literature and established assessment protocols.

quality_tiers.elite: 90-100 form_score: Competition-grade form, all criteria met
quality_tiers.good: 75-89 form_score: Minor deviations, one criterion slightly off
quality_tiers.average: 50-74 form_score: Multiple deviations, functional but not optimal
quality_tiers.poor: 0-49 form_score: Major form breakdowns, injury risk present

sources_overview: Cook G, et al. Functional Movement Screen (FMS) scoring criteria, 2006/2010
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed., 2016
Escamilla RF, et al. Biomechanics of the squat exercise, Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2001
Myer GD, et al. The back squat: a proposed assessment of functional deficits, SJMSS, 2014
Comfort P, et al. Standardization and methodological considerations for CMJ, Sports Med, 2019
Cogley RM, et al. Push-up variations EMG analysis, J Strength Cond Res, 2005
Youdas JW, et al. Push-up kinematics, J Strength Cond Res, 2010
Ronai P & Scibek E. Pull-up technique analysis, ACSM Health Fitness J, 2014
Suchomel TJ, et al. Weightlifting technique assessment, Sports Med, 2015
Ho KW, et al. Snatch kinematics, J Strength Cond Res, 2014
Bezodis IN, et al. Sprint biomechanics review, Sports Med, 2019
Bartlett RM. Javelin throw biomechanics, J Sports Sci, 1996
Stretch RA, et al. Cricket batting kinematics, J Sports Sci, 1998
Stuelcken MC, et al. Cricket batting biomechanics, Sports Biomech, 2005
Kritz M, et al. Movement competency screen, J Strength Cond Res, 2015

scoring_dimensions.name: countermovement_depth
scoring_dimensions.description: Knee flexion angle at lowest point of countermovement. Optimal loading position maximizes stretch-shortening cycle.

thresholds.elite: Knee flexion 80-100 deg, hip flexion 60-80 deg, smooth deceleration-to-acceleration transition
thresholds.good: Knee flexion 70-110 deg, hip flexion 50-90 deg, slight hesitation at bottom
thresholds.average: Knee flexion 60-120 deg OR <70 deg (shallow), inconsistent depth between trials
thresholds.poor: Knee flexion <50 deg (very shallow) or >130 deg (excessive), minimal countermovement use

scoring_dimensions.name: trunk_alignment
scoring_dimensions.description: Trunk inclination during countermovement and takeoff. Forward lean should be controlled and proportional.

thresholds.elite: Trunk forward lean 20-35 deg from vertical, maintained throughout, spine neutral
thresholds.good: Trunk forward lean 15-45 deg, slight rounding at bottom, recovers at takeoff
thresholds.average: Trunk forward lean >45 deg or <15 deg, some thoracic flexion
thresholds.poor: Excessive forward lean >60 deg, significant spinal flexion, lateral deviation

scoring_dimensions.name: knee_valgus_control
scoring_dimensions.description: Frontal plane knee alignment during takeoff and landing. Knee tracking over 2nd-3rd toe.

thresholds.elite: Knee-over-toe alignment within 5 deg of neutral, bilateral symmetry <3 deg difference
thresholds.good: Knee-over-toe alignment within 10 deg, bilateral symmetry <5 deg difference
thresholds.average: Mild valgus 10-15 deg, visible but controlled medial knee displacement
thresholds.poor: Valgus >15 deg, dynamic valgus collapse, significant bilateral asymmetry >10 deg

scoring_dimensions.name: arm_swing_coordination
scoring_dimensions.description: Bilateral arm swing timing and amplitude. Arms should drive upward synchronously at takeoff.

thresholds.elite: Full bilateral arm swing, shoulder flexion reaches >150 deg at takeoff, synchronized with triple extension
thresholds.good: Bilateral arm swing, shoulder flexion 120-150 deg, slight timing offset
thresholds.average: Reduced arm swing amplitude <120 deg, asymmetric swing, late timing
thresholds.poor: Minimal arm swing, arms stay at sides or move asynchronously, no contribution to jump

scoring_dimensions.name: triple_extension
scoring_dimensions.description: Simultaneous full extension of ankle, knee, and hip at takeoff. Key driver of jump height.

thresholds.elite: Full plantar flexion (ankle >140 deg), knee extension >170 deg, hip extension >170 deg at takeoff
thresholds.good: Near-full extension: ankle >130 deg, knee >160 deg, hip >160 deg
thresholds.average: Incomplete extension: one joint fails to reach threshold, knee or hip <155 deg
thresholds.poor: Significant flexion remaining at takeoff: knee <150 deg or hip <150 deg, no visible plantar flexion

scoring_dimensions.name: landing_mechanics
scoring_dimensions.description: Quality of landing: absorption strategy, knee alignment, and noise level.

thresholds.elite: Toe-to-heel landing, knee flexion >90 deg on absorption, silent/soft, no valgus, stable hold
thresholds.good: Toe-to-heel landing, knee flexion 70-90 deg, minor sound, controlled
thresholds.average: Flat-foot landing, knee flexion 50-70 deg, audible impact, slight valgus
thresholds.poor: Heel-strike landing, stiff legs (<50 deg flexion), loud impact, valgus collapse, loss of balance

common_faults: Dynamic knee valgus during takeoff or landing
Insufficient arm swing or asynchronous arm action
Excessive forward trunk lean causing horizontal displacement
Stiff landing with minimal knee/hip absorption

poor: Significant knee valgus detected -- strengthen hip abductors/external rotators
Very shallow countermovement -- practice depth loading at controlled speed
Landing is stiff and high-impact -- practice soft toe-to-heel landings
Minimal arm swing -- coordinate arm drive with leg extension
average: Countermovement depth slightly off optimal range -- aim for 90 deg knee flexion
Mild knee valgus present -- focus on tracking knees over toes
Arm swing timing is late -- initiate upswing earlier in concentric phase
Landing could be softer -- increase knee flexion on contact
good: Good overall jump mechanics -- minor timing refinement needed
Slight bilateral asymmetry in extension -- equalize push-off force
Landing is controlled but could absorb more through hips
elite: Excellent countermovement depth and timing
Full triple extension with coordinated arm drive
Textbook landing mechanics -- soft, stable, symmetric

vertical_jump.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score) where dimension_score = 100 - penalty. Penalty based on angular deviation from elite range midpoint: 0-5 deg deviation = 0-10 penalty, 5-15 deg = 10-30, 15-30 deg = 30-60, >30 deg = 60-100.
sources: Comfort P, et al. Standardization and methodological considerations for the countermovement jump, Sports Med, 2019
Myer GD, et al. Assessment of lower limb alignment during the CMJ, J Sports Sci, 2011
Lees A, et al. The biomechanics of jumping, J Sports Sci, 2004
FMS deep squat and hurdle step criteria (Cook et al., 2006)

scoring_dimensions.name: depth
scoring_dimensions.description: Hip crease position relative to knee. Gold standard is hip crease below top of patella for full squat.

thresholds.elite: Hip crease clearly below knee (thigh past parallel), knee flexion 110-130 deg, full depth with control
thresholds.good: Thigh parallel to floor (knee flexion 90-110 deg), hip crease at or slightly below knee level
thresholds.average: Partial squat, knee flexion 70-90 deg, above parallel
thresholds.poor: Quarter squat or less, knee flexion <70 deg, minimal hip displacement

scoring_dimensions.name: knee_tracking
scoring_dimensions.description: Frontal plane knee position. Knees should track over 2nd-3rd toe without collapsing inward.

thresholds.elite: Knees track over 2nd-3rd toe throughout, valgus <5 deg, bilateral symmetry
thresholds.good: Knees track over toes, mild valgus <10 deg only at deepest point, quickly corrected
thresholds.average: Intermittent valgus 10-15 deg, knees drift medially during ascent
thresholds.poor: Consistent valgus >15 deg, knees collapse inward, cannot maintain alignment

scoring_dimensions.name: trunk_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Trunk inclination relative to tibia. Excessive forward lean indicates poor thoracic mobility or weak extensors.

thresholds.elite: Trunk angle within 10 deg of tibia angle (parallel shins-torso), neutral spine throughout
thresholds.good: Trunk forward lean 5-15 deg more than tibia, neutral spine maintained
thresholds.average: Trunk forward lean 15-30 deg more than tibia, some thoracic rounding at depth
thresholds.poor: Trunk forward lean >30 deg beyond tibia, significant thoracic/lumbar flexion (butt wink)

scoring_dimensions.name: lumbar_spine_control
scoring_dimensions.description: Maintenance of neutral lumbar lordosis throughout movement. Excessive flexion ('butt wink') indicates risk.

thresholds.elite: Neutral lordosis maintained throughout full ROM, no visible flexion/extension change
thresholds.good: Neutral lordosis maintained to parallel, <10 deg flexion change at maximum depth
thresholds.average: Visible lumbar flexion 10-20 deg at depth, inconsistent control
thresholds.poor: Significant lumbar flexion >20 deg ('butt wink'), pain or compensatory movement

scoring_dimensions.name: heel_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Feet remain flat on ground. Heel rise indicates limited ankle dorsiflexion.

thresholds.elite: Heels flat throughout, ankle dorsiflexion >35 deg achieved
thresholds.good: Heels flat to parallel, minimal rise (<1 cm) at max depth only
thresholds.average: Heel rise >1 cm during descent, weight shifts forward
thresholds.poor: Significant heel rise throughout, comes onto toes, loses balance

scoring_dimensions.name: tempo_control
scoring_dimensions.description: Eccentric control and concentric drive. Movement should be controlled, not ballistic or collapsing.

thresholds.elite: Controlled 2-3 sec eccentric, brief pause at bottom, explosive concentric, no sticking point
thresholds.good: Controlled 2 sec eccentric, smooth reversal, slight deceleration at sticking point
thresholds.average: Fast uncontrolled eccentric (<1.5 sec), bounce at bottom, stalling in ascent
thresholds.poor: Dive-bomb eccentric, collapse at bottom, cannot reverse without momentum, ratcheting ascent

common_faults: Heel rise due to poor ankle dorsiflexion

poor: Significant knee valgus -- perform banded squats to activate glute medius
Major lumbar flexion at depth -- reduce depth until mobility improves
Heels rising off floor -- stretch calves and use heel elevation temporarily
Cannot reach parallel -- work on hip and ankle mobility
average: Depth is slightly above parallel -- work on hip flexor and ankle mobility
Some forward lean -- strengthen upper back and practice goblet squats
Minor butt wink at bottom -- reduce depth by 5-10 deg until mobility improves
Eccentric phase too fast -- practice tempo squats (3 sec down)
good: Good depth and alignment -- minor trunk lean correction needed
Slight valgus at max depth -- cue 'spread the floor' with feet
Strong overall pattern -- refine tempo for better control
elite: Full depth with neutral spine -- excellent mobility and control
Perfect knee tracking and bilateral symmetry
Exemplary squat pattern suitable for progressive loading

squat.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). dimension_score = max(0, 100 - angular_deviation_penalty - fault_penalty). angular_deviation_penalty: per degree outside elite range, deduct 2 points (linear). fault_penalty: knee_valgus >15 deg = -20, butt_wink >20 deg = -15, heel_rise = -10.
sources: Escamilla RF. Knee biomechanics of the dynamic squat exercise, Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2001
Myer GD, et al. The back squat: proposed assessment of functional deficits, Strength Cond J, 2014
Kritz M, et al. Movement competency screen, J Strength Cond Res, 2015
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed., Ch 15, 2016
Cook G, et al. FMS deep squat scoring criteria, 2006/2010
Schoenfeld BJ. Squat kinematics and kinetics, J Strength Cond Res, 2010

scoring_dimensions.name: elbow_angle_at_bottom
scoring_dimensions.description: Elbow flexion at the lowest point. Full ROM push-up requires chest near floor.

thresholds.elite: Elbow flexion to 90 deg or below (upper arm parallel or below parallel), chest within 5 cm of floor
thresholds.good: Elbow flexion 80-100 deg, chest within 10 cm of floor
thresholds.average: Elbow flexion 60-80 deg, partial ROM, chest >10 cm from floor
thresholds.poor: Elbow flexion <60 deg, very shallow movement, minimal displacement

scoring_dimensions.name: body_alignment
scoring_dimensions.description: Straight line from ankle through hip to shoulder. Core must remain rigid throughout.

thresholds.elite: Ear-shoulder-hip-knee-ankle in line throughout, hip sag/pike <5 deg deviation
thresholds.good: Near-straight line, hip sag or pike <10 deg at any point
thresholds.average: Visible hip sag 10-20 deg or hip pike 10-20 deg, inconsistent
thresholds.poor: Major hip sag >20 deg ('banana back') or pike >20 deg, low back hyperextension

scoring_dimensions.name: elbow_flare_angle
scoring_dimensions.description: Angle between upper arm and torso in transverse plane. Excessive flare stresses shoulder.

thresholds.elite: Upper arm 30-45 deg from torso (arrow position), scapulae retracted at bottom
thresholds.good: Upper arm 20-55 deg from torso, slight inconsistency between sides
thresholds.average: Upper arm 55-70 deg from torso ('T position'), increased shoulder stress
thresholds.poor: Upper arm >70 deg from torso (full T or beyond), shoulder impingement risk

scoring_dimensions.name: scapular_control
scoring_dimensions.description: Scapular movement quality: retraction at bottom, protraction at top. Winging indicates serratus weakness.

thresholds.elite: Full scapular retraction at bottom, protraction at top (plus push), no winging
thresholds.good: Adequate retraction/protraction, minimal winging, consistent pattern
thresholds.average: Incomplete scapular ROM, mild winging visible, inconsistent movement
thresholds.poor: Significant scapular winging, no retraction/protraction, shoulder elevation (shrugging)

scoring_dimensions.name: head_neck_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Cervical spine alignment. Head should remain neutral relative to thoracic spine.

thresholds.elite: Neutral cervical spine, gaze 30-60 cm ahead of hands, no chin jutting
thresholds.good: Near-neutral, slight forward gaze, chin stays tucked
thresholds.average: Head drops or extends, chin juts forward, gaze too far ahead or at floor
thresholds.poor: Severe cervical hyperextension or flexion, head leads movement

scoring_dimensions.name: tempo_consistency
scoring_dimensions.description: Consistent cadence and controlled movement. Fatigue shows as form degradation.

thresholds.elite: 1-2 sec eccentric, 1 sec concentric, consistent across all reps, full lockout
thresholds.good: Mostly consistent tempo, slight acceleration in later reps, full lockout
thresholds.average: Inconsistent tempo, rushing reps, incomplete lockout in some reps
thresholds.poor: Uncontrolled descent, bouncing off floor, no lockout, reps deteriorate rapidly

common_faults: Hip sag (anterior pelvic tilt, weak core)
Hip pike (compensation for weak pushing muscles)
Excessive elbow flare (>60 deg, shoulder stress)
Incomplete ROM (not reaching 90 deg elbow flexion)

poor: Major hip sag detected -- strengthen core with planks before push-ups
Very shallow range of motion -- use incline push-ups to build strength through full ROM
Elbows flaring to 90 deg -- tuck elbows to 45 deg to protect shoulders
Scapular winging present -- strengthen serratus anterior with wall slides
average: Some hip sag in later reps -- focus on bracing core before each rep
ROM slightly short of full depth -- lower chest closer to floor
Elbow flare angle too wide -- cue 'arrow not T' for arm position
Tempo inconsistent -- use a metronome for pacing
good: Good body alignment and depth -- minor elbow flare adjustment needed
Strong form overall -- add scapular protraction ('push plus') at top
Consistent reps with good control
elite: Full ROM with perfect alignment maintained
Optimal elbow position protecting shoulders
Excellent scapular mechanics and core stability

push_up.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). dimension_score = 100 - (deviation_deg / tolerance_deg) * max_penalty. tolerance_deg varies by dimension. Major faults (hip_sag >20 deg, elbow_flare >70 deg) apply additional -15 penalty each.
sources: Cogley RM, et al. Comparison of muscle activation using various hand positions during the push-up exercise, J Strength Cond Res, 2005
Youdas JW, et al. Surface EMG activation patterns and elbow joint motion during push-up, J Strength Cond Res, 2010
Suprak DN, et al. The effect of position on scapular kinematics during the push-up plus, J Biomech, 2013
ACE Personal Trainer Manual, 6th ed., 2020
NSCA Exercise Technique Guidelines, 2016

scoring_dimensions.name: range_of_motion
scoring_dimensions.description: Full ROM from dead hang (full elbow extension) to chin over bar. Incomplete ROM is the most common fault.

thresholds.elite: Full dead hang start (elbow extension >170 deg), chin clears bar by >5 cm, controlled return to full extension
thresholds.good: Near-full hang (elbow >160 deg), chin reaches bar level, controlled return
thresholds.average: Partial hang (elbow 140-160 deg), chin does not reach bar, incomplete descent
thresholds.poor: Very partial ROM (elbow <140 deg start), significant ROM cutting top and bottom

scoring_dimensions.name: scapular_engagement
scoring_dimensions.description: Initiation with scapular depression/retraction before elbow flexion. Shows lat activation vs. arm-dominant pull.

thresholds.elite: Clear scapular depression/retraction initiates pull, shoulders away from ears, lats visibly engaged
thresholds.good: Scapular engagement present but not pronounced, some shoulder elevation at start
thresholds.average: Minimal scapular engagement, pull initiated primarily by arms, shoulders shrug
thresholds.poor: No scapular engagement, full shoulder shrug throughout, arms-only pulling

scoring_dimensions.name: body_sway_control
scoring_dimensions.description: Minimal kipping, swinging, or lower body momentum. Strict pull-up requires controlled body position.

thresholds.elite: No visible swing, legs still or slightly forward, body moves vertically with <5 deg deviation
thresholds.good: Minimal swing <10 deg arc, slight leg movement, predominantly vertical path
thresholds.average: Moderate swing 10-20 deg arc, some kipping motion, legs swinging
thresholds.poor: Excessive kipping/swinging >20 deg arc, using momentum to clear bar

scoring_dimensions.name: grip_and_elbow_path
scoring_dimensions.description: Elbow path and grip position. Elbows should drive down toward hips, not flare laterally.

thresholds.elite: Elbows drive down and slightly back, grip shoulder-width, pronated grip consistent
thresholds.good: Elbows mostly track downward, minor flare at top, grip consistent
thresholds.average: Elbows flare outward, inconsistent path, grip width varies
thresholds.poor: Elbows flare significantly, chicken-wing pattern, grip slipping

scoring_dimensions.name: eccentric_control
scoring_dimensions.description: Controlled lowering phase. Dropping from top indicates insufficient strength for full control.

thresholds.elite: 2-3 sec controlled eccentric, smooth descent, full extension reached
thresholds.good: 1.5-2 sec eccentric, controlled but slightly faster, full extension
thresholds.average: 1-1.5 sec eccentric, partially controlled, may not reach full extension
thresholds.poor: <1 sec drop, no eccentric control, free-fall descent

scoring_dimensions.name: cervical_and_trunk_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Neck and trunk alignment. Chin-poking and excessive extension are compensations.

thresholds.elite: Neutral cervical spine, slight thoracic extension, no chin jutting to clear bar
thresholds.good: Mild chin forward at top to clear bar, trunk stable
thresholds.average: Noticeable chin jut, excessive thoracic extension/arching
thresholds.poor: Severe cervical hyperextension, excessive low back arching, head leads movement

common_faults: Incomplete ROM (not starting from dead hang or chin not reaching bar)
Chin jutting forward to 'reach' the bar

poor: Significant kipping/swinging -- use band-assisted strict pull-ups
Range of motion severely limited -- practice eccentric-only (slow negatives)
No scapular engagement -- practice scapular pull-ups as primer
Cannot control lowering -- build eccentric strength with 5-sec negatives
average: Chin not clearing bar consistently -- reduce band assistance gradually
Some body swing -- squeeze glutes and brace core to stabilize
Start from fuller hang -- pause at bottom for 1 sec each rep
Eccentric too fast -- slow descent to 2 sec minimum
good: Good ROM and control -- focus on scapular depression initiation
Minor swing at top -- maintain tighter core throughout
Strong pull pattern -- refine elbow path for lat emphasis
elite: Full ROM with excellent scapular mechanics
Perfect body control -- no swing, smooth vertical path
Outstanding eccentric control and strength balance

pull_up.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). dimension_score = 100 for meeting elite criteria, -3 per degree of kip/swing, -2 per degree of ROM shortfall from full range. Kipping >20 deg caps score at 40. Incomplete ROM (no chin over bar) caps score at 70.
sources: Ronai P & Scibek E. The pull-up, Strength Cond J, 2014
Youdas JW, et al. Surface EMG of latissimus dorsi and biceps during pull-up variations, J Strength Cond Res, 2010
Snarr RL & Esco MR. Electromyographical comparison of plank variations, J Strength Cond Res, 2014
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training, pull-up technique guidelines, 2016

scoring_dimensions.name: first_pull_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Bar path and body position from floor to knee. Back angle maintained, bar stays close.

thresholds.elite: Back angle constant (within 5 deg), bar within 3 cm of shins, knees clear bar path, shoulders over/slightly ahead of bar
thresholds.good: Back angle maintained within 10 deg, bar within 5 cm of shins, shoulders over bar
thresholds.average: Back angle changes 10-20 deg (hips rise fast), bar drifts 5-10 cm from body
thresholds.poor: Hips shoot up >20 deg change ('stripper pull'), bar drifts >10 cm, shoulders behind bar

scoring_dimensions.name: second_pull_explosion
scoring_dimensions.description: Triple extension at power position (bar at hip crease) with vertical bar acceleration. The primary force phase.

thresholds.elite: Full triple extension (hip >170 deg, knee >165 deg, ankle plantar flexion), bar-body contact at hip crease, vertical bar path
thresholds.good: Near-full extension, bar contacts hip, slight forward bar displacement <5 cm
thresholds.average: Incomplete hip extension (<160 deg), bar contact inconsistent, forward bar chase >5 cm
thresholds.poor: No full extension, arm pull dominates, bar loops forward >10 cm, 'muscle snatch' pattern

scoring_dimensions.name: third_pull_turnover
scoring_dimensions.description: Speed and position of pulling under the bar. Active pull-under vs. passive dropping.

thresholds.elite: Fast aggressive pull-under, elbows rotate high-to-locked in <0.3 sec, active push against bar
thresholds.good: Adequate turnover speed, elbows lock out overhead, slight press-out <15 deg
thresholds.average: Slow turnover, press-out 15-30 deg required, hesitation at catch
thresholds.poor: Very slow or no pull-under, major press-out >30 deg, power snatch height catch only

scoring_dimensions.name: overhead_catch_stability
scoring_dimensions.description: Receiving position quality. Bar over base of support, full depth, stable hold.

thresholds.elite: Bar directly over midfoot in sagittal plane, full overhead squat depth (hip below knee), stable 2-sec hold, arms locked
thresholds.good: Bar near midfoot (within 5 cm), squat to parallel, stable hold, arms locked
thresholds.average: Bar forward or behind midfoot >5 cm, above parallel catch, wobbly hold, some press-out
thresholds.poor: Bar significantly displaced, cannot stabilize overhead, steps forward/back to save, major balance loss

scoring_dimensions.name: bar_path_efficiency
scoring_dimensions.description: Overall bar trajectory. Ideal is slight S-curve close to body. Looping indicates technical error.

thresholds.elite: Slight S-curve, bar displacement <5 cm from vertical line through start, smooth acceleration profile
thresholds.good: Moderate S-curve, displacement 5-8 cm, consistent between reps
thresholds.average: Noticeable loop, displacement 8-15 cm, bar swings away from body
thresholds.poor: Large loop >15 cm, bar crashes overhead, inconsistent path between reps

scoring_dimensions.name: timing_rhythm
scoring_dimensions.description: Continuous fluid movement with proper phase transitions. No pausing or jerking between phases.

thresholds.elite: Seamless phase transitions, clear acceleration through second pull, rhythmic and repeatable
thresholds.good: Good rhythm with minor hesitation at transition point, mostly fluid
thresholds.average: Noticeable pause at knee or mid-thigh, segmented movement, inconsistent timing
thresholds.poor: Jerky, stop-and-go movement, no clear acceleration pattern, each rep different

common_faults: Early arm bend before full extension (arm pull snatch)
Hips rising faster than shoulders in first pull (stripper pull)
Bar looping forward away from body
No hip contact / missing second pull power position
Slow or absent third pull (passive drop under)
Catching forward on toes or stepping forward

poor: Arms bending too early -- keep arms straight until full hip extension
Hips shooting up first -- strengthen back and practice maintaining back angle
Bar looping far forward -- keep bar close with lats, practice high pulls
Cannot stabilize overhead -- build overhead squat and snatch balance progressions
average: Second pull not fully extending -- cue 'jump and shrug' at hip contact
Slow turnover -- practice tall snatches and snatch balances
Bar drifting forward -- focus on sweeping bar into hip crease
Catch position too high -- practice overhead squats for depth
good: Good overall lift -- refine bar path to stay closer to body
Minor press-out overhead -- strengthen lockout with snatch push press
Solid positions -- work on speed under the bar
elite: Excellent bar path efficiency and timing
Full extension with fast aggressive turnover
Stable deep overhead catch -- competition-ready technique

snatch.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). Key penalties: early_arm_bend = -15, bar_loop >15cm = -20, press_out >30deg = -15, no_hip_contact = -20, catch_instability (steps) = -10. Each penalty is binary (present/absent) or proportional to severity.
sources: Suchomel TJ, et al. The importance of muscular strength in athletic performance, Sports Med, 2016
Ho KW, et al. Kinematic analysis of the snatch in elite weightlifters, J Strength Cond Res, 2014
Gourgoulis V, et al. Snatch bar kinematics in elite weightlifters, J Sports Sci, 2009
Garhammer J. Biomechanical analysis of Olympic weightlifting, Med Sci Sports Exerc, 1985
Kipp K, et al. Mechanical demands of the snatch and clean, Sports Biomech, 2012
IWF Technical Officials Judging Criteria (press-out, incomplete extension)

scoring_dimensions.name: acceleration_posture
scoring_dimensions.description: Body lean during initial acceleration phase (0-30m). Requires forward lean with progressive rise.

thresholds.elite: 45-55 deg forward lean at start, progressive rise to upright by 25-30m, straight line head-to-ankle
thresholds.good: 40-60 deg at start, upright by 30-35m, mostly linear body position
thresholds.average: Upright too early (<20m) or too much lean (>60 deg), body position inconsistent
thresholds.poor: Near-vertical at start or excessive lean >65 deg, no progressive transition

scoring_dimensions.name: knee_drive_height
scoring_dimensions.description: Maximum thigh angle during swing phase at top speed. Reflects hip flexor power and sprint mechanics.

thresholds.elite: Thigh reaches parallel or above (hip flexion >90 deg), knee drive height at hip level
thresholds.good: Thigh within 10 deg of parallel (hip flexion 80-90 deg)
thresholds.average: Thigh 20-30 deg below parallel (hip flexion 60-80 deg), low knee drive
thresholds.poor: Minimal knee lift, thigh well below parallel (hip flexion <60 deg), shuffling pattern

scoring_dimensions.name: foot_strike_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Ground contact position relative to center of mass. Overstriding increases braking forces.

thresholds.elite: Foot contacts ground directly under or slightly behind COM, dorsiflexed ankle, forefoot strike
thresholds.good: Foot contacts within 5 cm ahead of COM, forefoot/midfoot strike
thresholds.average: Foot contacts 5-15 cm ahead of COM, midfoot to mild heel strike, visible braking
thresholds.poor: Overstriding >15 cm ahead of COM, heel strike, significant braking force visible

scoring_dimensions.name: arm_action
scoring_dimensions.description: Arm swing mechanics. Elbows at ~90 deg, driving from shoulder, hands relaxed, cheek-to-hip range.

thresholds.elite: Elbow angle 85-95 deg, hands reach cheek height and hip pocket, relaxed hands, no cross-body rotation
thresholds.good: Elbow angle 80-100 deg, slightly reduced range, minimal cross-body movement
thresholds.average: Elbow angle variable, arms cross midline, hands tense/fisted, reduced drive
thresholds.poor: Arms flailing, excessive cross-body rotation, elbows straightening, hands clenched

scoring_dimensions.name: hip_extension_at_toe_off
scoring_dimensions.description: Full hip extension during push-off. Incomplete extension reduces stride power.

thresholds.elite: Hip extension >200 deg (past neutral, 20+ deg behind vertical), full ankle plantar flexion at toe-off
thresholds.good: Hip extension 190-200 deg, near-full ankle push-off
thresholds.average: Hip extension 180-190 deg (near neutral), incomplete push-off
thresholds.poor: Hip extension <180 deg (never reaches full extension), abbreviated push-off

scoring_dimensions.name: pelvic_stability
scoring_dimensions.description: Frontal and transverse plane pelvic control. Excessive drop or rotation wastes energy.

thresholds.elite: Pelvic drop <5 deg, transverse rotation <10 deg, stable pelvis throughout stride
thresholds.good: Pelvic drop 5-8 deg, rotation 10-15 deg, mostly stable
thresholds.average: Pelvic drop 8-12 deg, rotation 15-25 deg, visible hip sway
thresholds.poor: Pelvic drop >12 deg (Trendelenburg), rotation >25 deg, waddling gait pattern

common_faults: Heel striking during max velocity phase
Upright too early in acceleration phase
Tense upper body (clenched fists, raised shoulders)

poor: Severe overstriding detected -- shorten stride length, focus on turnover rate
Very low knee drive -- practice A-skips and high-knee drills
Arms crossing body significantly -- practice arm action drills in mirror
Heel striking -- drill forefoot contacts with wall drives
average: Moderate overstriding -- cue 'pull the ground under you'
Knee drive below parallel -- add hip flexor strength work and A-skips
Some cross-body arm action -- run with hands open and relaxed
Rising too early in acceleration -- hold lean longer, push for 20m
good: Good foot strike positioning -- refine dorsiflexion timing
Solid knee drive -- push for slightly higher thigh position
Minor pelvic rotation -- strengthen lateral core stability
elite: Excellent foot strike under COM with full dorsiflexion
Powerful knee drive at or above parallel
Textbook acceleration-to-upright transition

sprint.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). overstriding_penalty = distance_ahead_of_COM_cm * 2 (capped at 30). knee_drive_penalty = max(0, (90 - hip_flexion_deg)) * 1.5. heel_strike_penalty = 15 (binary). cross_body_arms = 10.
sources: Bezodis IN, et al. Sprint running biomechanics, Sports Med, 2019
Mann R & Herman J. Kinematic analysis of sprint running, Med Sci Sports, 1985
Clark KP & Weyand PG. Sprint running mechanics, J Exp Biol, 2014
Haugen T, et al. Sprint running mechanics in elite athletes, Int J Sports Physiol Perform, 2019
Nagahara R, et al. Kinematics of transition during sprint acceleration, J Sports Sci, 2014
NSCA Sprint technique evaluation guidelines, 2016

scoring_dimensions.name: approach_run_rhythm
scoring_dimensions.description: Progressive acceleration over approach run with controlled crossover steps. Final steps establish rhythm.

thresholds.elite: Smooth acceleration, consistent stride length, seamless transition into crossover steps, optimal velocity at plant
thresholds.good: Good acceleration, minor rhythm disruption at crossover transition
thresholds.average: Inconsistent stride length, noticeable deceleration entering crossover steps
thresholds.poor: Irregular approach, major deceleration, stuttering steps, poor rhythm

scoring_dimensions.name: withdrawal_and_carry
scoring_dimensions.description: Javelin withdrawal timing and arm position during crossover steps. Javelin should be drawn back early and aligned with shoulder.

thresholds.elite: Early withdrawal (2-3 steps before plant), javelin aligned with throwing shoulder, palm up, elbow at shoulder height
thresholds.good: Timely withdrawal, javelin near alignment, elbow slightly low or high
thresholds.average: Late withdrawal (1 step before plant), javelin off-axis, elbow drops below shoulder
thresholds.poor: No clear withdrawal phase, javelin poorly positioned, wrapping behind body

scoring_dimensions.name: block_leg_brace
scoring_dimensions.description: Front (block) leg action at delivery. Firm block converts horizontal to vertical/rotational energy.

thresholds.elite: Block leg plants ahead of COM at 155-170 deg knee extension, firm brace with <10 deg collapse, COM vaults over
thresholds.good: Block leg at 145-155 deg, minor collapse 10-15 deg, adequate energy transfer
thresholds.average: Block leg at 130-145 deg, collapses 15-25 deg, soft block, energy leaks
thresholds.poor: Block leg <130 deg (bent), collapses >25 deg, no blocking action, 'throwing off bent leg'

scoring_dimensions.name: hip_shoulder_separation
scoring_dimensions.description: Rotational separation between hip and shoulder axes at plant. Key driver of elastic energy storage.

thresholds.elite: Hip-shoulder separation 40-55 deg at front foot plant, hips lead rotation, sequential unwinding
thresholds.good: Separation 30-40 deg, hips lead but less stored elastic energy
thresholds.average: Separation 15-30 deg, hips and shoulders rotate together (block rotation)
thresholds.poor: Separation <15 deg or shoulders lead hips, no separation, 'arm throw'

scoring_dimensions.name: release_angle_and_point
scoring_dimensions.description: Javelin release angle and release point relative to shoulder. Optimal release ~33-36 deg for elite.

thresholds.elite: Release angle 33-36 deg, release point over front foot at maximum shoulder height, javelin axis aligned with trajectory
thresholds.good: Release angle 30-38 deg, release point slightly early or late, minor axis deviation
thresholds.average: Release angle 25-30 or 38-45 deg, release point well behind or over front foot, javelin wobble
thresholds.poor: Release angle <25 or >45 deg, very early/late release, javelin unstable, significant wobble

scoring_dimensions.name: follow_through_recovery
scoring_dimensions.description: Deceleration after release without fouling. Controlled forward momentum dissipation.

thresholds.elite: Aggressive follow-through with reverse (rear leg swaps forward), stops well before line, balanced
thresholds.good: Follow-through with reverse, stops before line, minor balance adjustment
thresholds.average: Abbreviated follow-through, stumbles forward, near the line
thresholds.poor: No follow-through (decelerating before release), or foul past line, falls forward

common_faults: Soft block leg (bending front knee on delivery)
Release angle too flat or too steep
Javelin not aligned with throwing direction (cross-body)
Elbow dropping below shoulder at release

poor: Throwing with arm only -- practice standing throws focusing on hip rotation
Block leg collapsing -- strengthen front leg with single-leg exercises
Release angle far from optimal -- practice release point with towel drills
No javelin withdrawal -- practice crossover steps with withdrawal separately
average: Hip-shoulder separation insufficient -- practice rotational medicine ball throws
Block leg too soft -- cue 'brace hard on front leg'
Release angle slightly off -- adjust aim point upward/downward
Approach rhythm breaking down -- simplify to 3-step approach first
good: Good hip-shoulder separation -- refine timing for more elastic energy
Solid block leg -- push for firmer brace to maximize transfer
Strong throw pattern -- fine-tune release angle to 33-36 deg window
elite: Excellent kinetic chain sequencing from ground up
Optimal release angle and point with full hip-shoulder separation
Competition-ready technique with controlled follow-through

javelin.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). Key penalties: no_hip_shoulder_separation = -25, soft_block (collapse >25deg) = -20, release_angle deviation from 34.5 midpoint: per deg = -2.5. Arm-only throw (separation <15 deg) caps score at 35.
sources: Bartlett RM. The biomechanics of the javelin throw: a review, J Sports Sci, 1996
Mero A, et al. Biomechanics of javelin throwing, Sports Med, 1994
Liu H, et al. Kinematic analysis of elite javelin throwers, J Sports Sci Med, 2010
Whiting WC, et al. Javelin release parameters, J Applied Biomech, 1991
Campos J, et al. Kinematic analysis of the javelin throw at the IAAF World Championships, New Studies Athletics, 2004

scoring_dimensions.name: backlift
scoring_dimensions.description: Bat position and path during backswing. High backlift with face pointing toward slips (traditional) or straighter path.

thresholds.elite: Bat raised to stump height or above, face angled toward point/slips, hands near back shoulder, smooth continuous lift
thresholds.good: Bat raised to hip-stump height, face near correct angle, hands at shoulder, mostly smooth
thresholds.average: Low backlift (bat below hip), face angle incorrect (closed/open), hands low
thresholds.poor: Minimal or no backlift, bat stays near pad, no loading of swing, or excessive bat wrap behind body

scoring_dimensions.name: head_and_eye_position
scoring_dimensions.description: Head position relative to front knee at contact. Still head enables visual tracking of ball.

thresholds.elite: Head still and level, eyes level, head over front knee at contact (front foot shots), weight transfers smoothly
thresholds.good: Head mostly still, slight movement, eyes level, head near front knee
thresholds.average: Head moves laterally or up/down, eyes tilting, head behind front knee
thresholds.poor: Significant head movement, falling away from ball, eyes off level, no weight transfer

scoring_dimensions.name: front_foot_stride
scoring_dimensions.description: Front foot movement toward pitch of ball. Stride length and direction indicate intent and balance.

thresholds.elite: Stride to pitch of ball, front foot lands in line with ball, knee flexion 130-150 deg at contact, balanced
thresholds.good: Good stride length, foot lands near line of ball, knee slightly stiff or over-bent
thresholds.average: Short stride or off-line, foot not reaching pitch, planting too early or late
thresholds.poor: No stride (stuck in crease), lunging, falling over, foot nowhere near ball line

scoring_dimensions.name: bat_swing_plane
scoring_dimensions.description: Downswing path of bat. Should come down straight toward ball then follow through. Cross-bat vs straight bat.

thresholds.elite: Straight bat coming from close to body, bat face presented full to ball, wrists firm through contact zone, bat comes down from high to low on line of ball
thresholds.good: Mostly straight bat, minor deviation from ideal plane, bat face slightly open/closed at contact
thresholds.average: Bat deviating from straight plane, playing across the line, bat face angled at contact
thresholds.poor: Cross-bat to straight delivery, bat face completely open/closed, playing around front pad

scoring_dimensions.name: contact_point_timing
scoring_dimensions.description: Where ball is contacted relative to body. Under eyes is ideal for defense, slightly in front for drives.

thresholds.elite: Contact under eyes (defense) or 30-50 cm in front of pad (drives), correct for shot type, middle of bat
thresholds.good: Contact near optimal zone, within 10 cm of ideal, slight mistiming occasionally
thresholds.average: Contact too early (reaching) or too late (cramped), 10-20 cm from ideal zone
thresholds.poor: Severely early or late, >20 cm from optimal contact zone, edging or missing frequently

scoring_dimensions.name: follow_through_and_balance
scoring_dimensions.description: Completion of stroke and post-shot balance. Full follow-through with maintained balance indicates controlled shot.

thresholds.elite: Full follow-through with high elbow finish, weight balanced, could hold finish position, head still
thresholds.good: Good follow-through, minor balance adjustment after shot, head mostly still
thresholds.average: Abbreviated follow-through, off-balance, falling to one side, head moves
thresholds.poor: No follow-through, completely off balance, falling away, cannot recover for next ball

common_faults: Playing across the line (cross-bat to straight deliveries)
Head falling over to off side (losing sight of ball)
No front foot stride (batting from crease, flat-footed)
Bat face not presented to ball (angled face at contact)
Playing too early or too late (timing)
Bottom hand dominant (closing face, reduced control)
Hard hands (no give, edges carry to slips)
Front foot not to pitch of ball

poor: Playing across the line consistently -- practice straight bat drills with guide rope
Head falling away from ball -- do bobble feed drills focusing on watching ball to bat
No front foot movement -- practice stride drills with target mat
Bat face not presenting to ball -- do shadow batting focusing on wrist position
average: Backlift too low -- raise hands higher in stance for better bat speed
Stride not reaching pitch of ball -- practice getting front foot further forward
Timing slightly off -- use bowling machine at consistent speed to groove timing
Bottom hand too dominant -- practice top-hand-only batting drills
good: Good overall technique -- refine bat face presentation at contact
Solid head position -- keep weight transfer slightly more forward
Strong batting foundation -- focus on follow-through completion
elite: Textbook head position and weight transfer
Excellent bat swing plane and timing
Full controlled follow-through with perfect balance

cricket_bat.form_score_formula: form_score = sum(dimension_weight * dimension_score). Key penalties: cross_bat_to_straight = -25, head_falling_away = -20, no_stride = -15, bat_face_angle deviation >15 deg = -10. Playing across the line on defensive shots caps score at 40.
sources: Stretch RA, et al. A biomechanical analysis of the batting backlift, J Sports Sci, 1998
Stuelcken MC, et al. The biomechanics of batting in cricket, Sports Biomech, 2005
Taliep MS, et al. Bat-ball contact conditions for skilled cricket batting, J Sports Sci, 2007
Cork A, et al. Kinematic analysis of cricket batting, J Sports Sci, 2010
Abernethy B & Russell DG. Expert-novice differences in cricket batting, J Sport Psychol, 1984
ECB Coaching Manual: Technical Assessment of Batting, England and Wales Cricket Board
Woolmer B, et al. Bob Woolmer's Art and Science of Cricket, 2008

score_computation.description: Universal scoring algorithm applicable across all movements

algorithm.step_1: For each scoring dimension, determine raw dimension score (0-100) based on which threshold tier the observed values fall into: elite range = 85-100, good range = 65-84, average range = 35-64, poor range = 0-34
algorithm.step_2: Within each tier, interpolate linearly based on proximity to next tier boundary. E.g., top of 'good' range scores 84, bottom scores 65
algorithm.step_3: Apply dimension weights: weighted_score = sum(dimension_weight_i * dimension_score_i)
algorithm.step_4: Apply fault penalties: for each detected major fault, subtract fixed penalty from total (sport-specific penalties listed per movement)
algorithm.step_5: Apply hard caps: certain severe faults cap maximum achievable score (e.g., kipping >20 deg on pull-up caps at 40)
algorithm.step_7: Assign quality tier label: 90-100 = elite, 75-89 = good, 50-74 = average, 0-49 = poor

angle_deviation_penalty_schedule.description: Default penalty schedule for angular deviations from elite midpoint, used when sport-specific formula not defined

bilateral_asymmetry_penalty.description: Additional penalty for left-right differences in bilateral movements (squat, push-up, vertical jump)
